definitions.E: L-n*d >= 0, total incidence surplus above minimum degree
definitions.e_y: deg(y)-d for a nonpivot variable y; e_y>=0 and the nonpivot e_y sum equals E because the selected pivot itself has degree d
definitions.t_y: retained-clause incidence count of nonpivot variable y
definitions.u_y: number of the d pivot-parent clauses omitting y
definitions.J: new distinct non-tautological resolvents not already in retained raw set

statement: For every nonpivot y, total degree is d+e_y. It occurs t_y times in retained clauses, hence d+e_y-t_y times in the d pivot-parent clauses and is omitted from exactly u_y=t_y-e_y parent clauses.
Summing over nonpivot variables gives sum_y u_y = T-E.
Split u_y=a_y+b_y across the positive and negative parent buckets. Then a_y*b_y<=u_y^2/4<=c*u_y/4 because 0<=u_y<=t_y<=c.
Therefore total pair-support mass obeys S >= r*p*q-floor(c*(T-E)/4), where r=n-1.

If J new distinct resolvents are added to c retained clauses, those c+J clauses are distinct. Their J representative resolvents have total width <=Wmax_r(c+J)-T, and the remaining p*q-J pair supports are each <=r. Thus S<=Wmax_r(c+J)-T+(p*q-J)r.
At a normalized unit-free stage, T lies in the integer interval max(2c,E)<=T<=min(c*r,L-2d) for c>0; c=0 has T=0. Maximizing the feasible J over this interval is an exact theorem-side ceiling.
relation_to_regular_lemma: The previous regular-incidence theorem is exactly the special case E=0.
